teams.heading: Jake White named Fiji head coach, replacing interim Senirusi Seruvakula
teams.body: Jake White has been named Fiji head coach, succeeding interim coach Senirusi Seruvakula, after being chosen from 31 applicants last week. The 62-year-old was the Bulls' director of rugby from 2020 to 2025, and former Bulls colleagues believe Fiji have found the right man. White inherits a team ranked 10th in the world that has lost four of five Tests this year, and his first match in charge is against Japan. Fiji sit in Pool C at the 2027 World Cup.

lead.why: The head coach appointment is the biggest men's national-team item in the pack, and it has not been covered in the previous editions.

teams.heading: George Hendy and Will Butt press Borthwick's case with Champions Cup displays
teams.body: Planet Rugby's view after round one of the Champions Cup is that Borthwick has a selection puzzle on his hands, with the wings the pressing issue. Northampton's George Hendy, who scored against Cardiff, and Exeter's Will Butt, who had Toulouse's backline on toast in France, both made telling cases, while Gloucester's Seb Atkinson and Arthur Clark also stood out. England may be looking for a winger to emerge given injury concerns in that department, and Hendy has done his prospects no harm.

lead.why: A new men's national-team selection story that the Feyi-Waboso items already read this week don't cover.

teams.heading: Théo Attissogbe inspires Pau club to 41-17 Champions Cup win over Leicester
teams.body: In a Champions Cup club match, Pau beat Leicester 41-17 at Stade du Hameau, with France star Théo Attissogbe central to the hosts' turnaround. Pau trailed 10-3 after 18 minutes and led only 17-10 at half-time, before outscoring Leicester 24-7 after the break. Planet Rugby's takeaways credit Attissogbe's 'moments of magic' for the change in momentum, and suggest Pau could be dark horses for the rest of the competition.

teams.heading: Ex-Scotland captain Jamie Ritchie set for club debut with Glasgow against Benetton
teams.body: Glasgow have set up the club debut of Jamie Ritchie, the former Scotland captain who signed from Perpignan over the summer, with assistant coach Nigel Carolan saying the time has come to "unleash" him. Ritchie has been sidelined by ankle and Achilles tendon problems and summer surgery, but is back in full training and expected to play against Benetton in Treviso, either starting or on the bench. The 30-year-old, capped 63 times, spent 11 years at Edinburgh before moving to Scotstoun on a two-year deal.

teams.heading: Wales add match official Ben Whitehouse as full-time specialist coach under Tandy
teams.body: Wales have added a match official to the national set-up, with the WRU confirming on Monday that Ben Whitehouse has joined Steve Tandy's men's squad full-time as a specialist coach. The 36-year-old is set to hang up his whistle after Saturday's URC clash between the Ospreys and Dragons in Swansea. According to the WRU, he will work with coaches and players on law, discipline, decision-making and communication, a role that echoes Jaco Peyper's laws adviser post with Rassie Erasmus' Springboks.

teams.heading: Victor Matfield says Wallabies 'definitely not top four' before home World Cup
teams.body: Springboks legend Victor Matfield says the Wallabies are not one of the world's best five sides and doubts they will reach the 2027 World Cup semi-finals. "They're definitely not top four. I don't even think top five," he said. Australia are currently seventh in the rankings, having dropped below Scotland after back-to-back Bledisloe Cup defeats to the All Blacks. Sir John Kirwan, on the Rivals Rugby podcast, said: "I just can't get a read on them."

teams.heading: Club Shizuoka Blue Revs confirm Kwagga Smith contract termination by mutual agreement
teams.body: The Shizuoka Blue Revs have parted ways with Springboks flanker Kwagga Smith by mutual agreement, the club confirmed on Tuesday, amid reports he is heading back to South Africa. The club captain in recent seasons played 81 matches for them and was named the league's Player of the Season in 2023. Rassie Erasmus has previously said Smith is unlikely to recover from a knee injury in time for the November Nations Championship.

Former All Black Mils Muliaina argues the run of injuries has been a positive, saying "it's promising because we've got depth". teams.heading: Kwagga Smith's Blue Revs contract terminated as South African return rumours build
teams.body: Kwagga Smith's time at Shizuoka Blue Revs is over, with the club confirming on Tuesday that his contract was terminated by mutual agreement. The 33-year-old, once club captain, has been linked with the Bulls, and Johan Ackermann has confirmed interest in bringing him home. For the Springboks the timing is awkward: Smith has been sidelined by a knee injury that has kept him out of every international this season, and Erasmus has said he is unlikely to be fit for the November Nations Championship.

lead.why: A concrete, confirmed event: Smith's contract has ended, and the knee injury puts his November availability in doubt.
